proposals.title: Require an assay and expression transformation contract before model comparison
proposals.claim: A loader contract that records assay, panel and expression transformation will detect representation-invalid artifacts before any model score is interpreted.
proposals.mechanism: de_score and mmd_u can change under expression transformation alone. Check supplied normalized .X, panel order and scorer preprocessing; reject unsupported raw-count reconstruction. This is a validation gate, not an asserted score gain.
proposals.falsifier: On genuine released files plus deliberately centered and panel-reordered copies, kill the gate if it misses either invalid copy or rejects a documented valid representation.

evidence.says: _dense reads .X directly; validation checks finite nonnegative entries and panel order at line 128.

evidence.ref: Hafemeister and Satija, Genome Biology 2019, doi:10.1186/s13059-019-1874-1; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6927181/
evidence.says: Regularized UMI depth models address technical variation; unconstrained count models can overfit biological variance.

proposals.title: Diagnose mixture and state errors using independent sample-aware baselines
proposals.claim: A proportion-only versus within-type-state-only baseline comparison will distinguish mixture-driven from conditional-expression-driven improvements in released-stage proxies.
proposals.mechanism: de_direction and mmd_u can reflect cell mixture as well as cell state. Hold one component fixed, evaluate pooled and conditional discrepancies, and repeat sample-balanced draws instead of taking the first 150 rows.
proposals.falsifier: With released data, kill the diagnostic if controlled proportion-only and state-only changes are indistinguishable under its conditional reports across repeated sample-balanced draws.

evidence.says: Proxy score uses at most 150 cells selected from initial rows of candidate, truth and reference.
Cells sharing an embryo/sample must not be treated as independent biological replicates.

evidence.ref: Squair et al., Nature Communications 2021, doi:10.1038/s41467-021-25960-2; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-25960-2.pdf
evidence.says: Accounting for biological replicates prevents false differential-expression discoveries in examined datasets.
